content.user_title: Dispatch Parallel Agents for Independent Tasks
content.value_statement: Independent coding failures slow teams when one agent investigates everything in sequence. This skill shows how to split work into focused parallel agent tasks.
actual_capabilities: Explains when multiple failures are independent enough for parallel agent work.
Shows how to scope each agent to one test file or subsystem.
Provides prompt structure for focused debugging tasks.
Describes review and integration steps after agents return.
Lists common mistakes, constraints, and verification checks.
limitations: Does not create or manage agents by itself.
Assumes work can be separated without shared state.
Uses examples centered on coding and test failures.
Requires human review to merge results and catch conflicts.

use_cases.title: Triage Independent Test Failures
use_cases.description: Split unrelated failing test files into separate agent tasks with clear goals and constraints.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Multi-Agent Debugging
use_cases.description: Assign narrow problem domains to several coding agents, then review their summaries before integration.

use_cases.title: Design Focused Agent Prompts
use_cases.description: Turn broad debugging work into self-contained prompts that include scope, context, and expected output.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Task Independence
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner triage before using parallel agents.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to decide whether these tasks can run in parallel: [list tasks]. Group related work, identify dependencies, and recommend one agent plan.

prompt_templates.title: Create Agent Assignments
prompt_templates.scenario: Prepare focused tasks for separate agents.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create parallel agent assignments for these independent failures: [failure list]. For each assignment, include scope, goal, constraints, and expected summary.

prompt_templates.title: Review Returned Fixes
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these agent summaries: [summaries]. Identify conflicts, missing verification, and the safest order for applying or validating the changes.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize a Multi-Agent Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow design for a larger debugging session.
prompt_templates.prompt: Given this project state and failure map: [context]. Design a parallel agent plan, define boundaries, flag shared-state risks, and provide an integration checklist.

output_examples.input: Three unrelated test files fail after a refactor.
output: Groups failures into abort logic, batch completion, and approval timing.
Recommends one agent per file with strict file scope.
Adds a final full-suite verification step.

output_examples.input: An agent plan includes two tasks that edit the same module.
output: Flags the tasks as unsafe for parallel execution.
Suggests a sequential investigation or a narrower split by ownership.
Adds conflict checks before merging any result.

output_examples.input: A broad prompt says to fix all failing tests.
output: Rewrites the work into scoped agent prompts.
Adds context, constraints, and expected summaries for each agent.
Keeps integration review with the primary user.

best_practices: Dispatch agents only after confirming tasks are independent.
Give each agent one scope, one goal, and clear constraints.
Review summaries and run the full test suite before integration.
anti_patterns: Sending one agent a broad request to fix everything.
Running agents in parallel when they must edit shared files.
Accepting agent changes without conflict review or verification.

faq.question: Does this skill run parallel agents automatically?
faq.answer: No. It explains how to decide, scope, dispatch, review, and integrate parallel agent work.

faq.question: When should I avoid this workflow?
faq.answer: Avoid it when failures are related, require full-system context, or need changes in the same files.

faq.question: Can I use it outside test debugging?
faq.answer: Yes. Use it for independent coding tasks, documentation checks, or subsystem reviews with clear boundaries.

faq.question: What should each agent receive?
faq.answer: Each agent should receive one scope, clear context, constraints, and the expected summary format.

faq.question: How do I reduce merge conflicts?
faq.answer: Separate tasks by file, subsystem, or ownership, then review all summaries before applying changes together.
